The sheet stayed open for over a minute until closed, greying the map. The original shows no dialog. Round 7 ran the same keyboard flow under load and did not report this. confirmed.suspectedCause: Sift's popup or dialog finder (or the new field-panel logic around fieldList/fieldPanel/panelList in src/content/index.ts) takes a page container near the focused search box for an opened dialog. This happens while Google is still settling after the focus: the #gb Google bar in a fixed header, or the filter chip bar. Sift then shows it as a modal and moves focus into it.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. I used a fresh tab (SIFT_TAB=skeptic) with Google Maps coffee search, 1280x900, and 4x CPU throttle. First run of gdlg.ts with mouse focus: 5 of 6 trials showed a Sift .layer reading 'Close | Google apps | Sign in' 0.6 to 3.7 s after focus. A second run gave 1 of 5 mouse trials and 3 of 5 keyboard (Shift+Tab) trials. Controls showed nothing: no focus at 4x was 0 of 4, and unthrottled at load average 1 was 0 of 4. I also ran my own typing trace (gtype.ts: click, then type 'Coit Tower' key by key). In 1 of 5 trials the layer appeared right after the click. Focus ended on button(Close), the page field ended as 'coTowerffee' so 'Coit ' was lost, and the sheet then showed 'Close | Price | Rating | Hours | All filters' over a greyed page. Original control (Sift off, 4x): the same typing went into the field, Google showed only its suggestion list, and there was no dialog. It is intermittent and only shows under CPU pressure. When it hits, it is a real input-loss bug and is caused by Sift. Note: one keyboard run I first made had Sift switched off by an earlier control; I threw it away and reran it with Sift on.
confirmed.fix: src/content/extract/generic.ts findPopup()/popupLike(): do not take a positioned container as a popup the action opened when it was on screen before the action. Record visible fixed/absolute boxes when arming, beyond armShown, which only holds what Sift showed. Also reject it when its controls are already in Sift's page view (the chip bar) or when it is the site's account bar (#gb, which has a 'Google apps'/'Sign in' link). In src/content/index.ts, do not move focus into a newly opened sheet while the user is typing in a field they just entered.

confirmed.where: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String/toUpperCase (Browser compatibility > Settings); likely every MDN page with a compat table
confirmed.evidence: Clicking Sift's 'Settings' button opens MDN's native 'Browser compatibility settings' modal (a dialog in mdn-compat-table-lazy's shadow root). A click on the Bun chip's × changes nothing. While it is open, a click on a Sift link (String.prototype.toLowerCase()) does nothing, and a click on the Sift switch does nothing. Tab moves focus from the modal's close button to <body>. Only Escape closes it. Desktop Chrome Edge Firefox Safari Internet Explorer Opera Mobil…'. On the original (Sift off), the same real clicks open the modal, and Cancel closes it (open dialogs 0). Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-3/research/shots/R8-T3-mdn-settings-sift.png, /home/nico/projects/sift-test-3/research/shots/R8-T3-mdn-compat-orig.png

Original control: bun scripts/act.ts press:Alt+Shift+S; bun $S/r8t3/mdnsettings-orig.ts  (after Cancel: open dialogs: 0); bun scripts/act.ts press:Alt+Shift+S.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The page opens a showModal() dialog inside nested shadow roots. Sift's dialog detection does not see it, so it is not mirrored in Sift's sheet. The dialog enters the top layer above Sift's popover, but the shield keeps the page inert, so its controls get no clicks, and its backdrop covers Sift.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice on String/toUpperCase. A real click on Sift's Settings opens MDN's native modal over Sift (open dialogs: 1). Real clicks on its Cancel (817,692) and Save (882,692) leave it open. On the original (Sift off, Settings scrolled into view, real clicks) Cancel closes it (open dialogs: 0). Cause, checked in the DOM: the dialog sits in mdn-modal's shadow root, but Cancel, Save, the browser chips and the footer are mdn-modal's slotted light-DOM children. The Cancel mdn-button is not inside the dialog per dialog.contains(), and its closest [inert] is a footer marked data-sift-inert. Sift's shield exempts only the dialog and its ancestors, so the slotted controls stay inert, and no pointer or click event reached Cancel. Two corrections to the report. First, the modal's own close X (898,199, inside the shadow dialog) does close it, so Escape is not the only way out. Second, Sift's links and switch not working while a page modal is open is the intended design (index.ts: a page modal blocks everything else, as on the original). The real defect is that the modal's own main controls do nothing.
confirmed.fix: src/content/shield.ts desired(): do not mark a child whose assigned slot (following assignedSlot up the chain) lies inside an exempted element (composed-tree containment). Or, in index.ts refreshModals()/exempt(), exempt the shadow host that holds the modal dialog (mdn-modal), so its slotted content stays usable.

confirmed.suspectedCause: After the page renders the code there is no prompt re-extraction: the next run comes about 2 s later, or the runs right after the code appears do not yet read it, perhaps because the code view is still marked as loading.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced, but the cause is not scheduling, and I rate it medium, not high. fp2.ts at load average about 1 gave original vs Sift: 2057/2809, 822/1582, 1133/1831, 1289/1912 and 1139/1808 ms. Sift was later in 5 of 5. Poll traces show .react-code-lines with the code text at 742 to 942 ms, and Sift adding the code only at 2521 to 2632 ms, while runs 4 to 6 in between stayed at 285 chars. Why: GitHub's visible code container (div.react-code-file-contents) is aria-hidden=true, and Sift skips aria-hidden content (generic.ts around line 3414). Sift waits for the screen-reader textarea #read-only-cursor-text-area, which GitHub mounts at about 2.6 s. Sift shows the code in the same run that textarea appears. So code a sighted user sees on the original after about 0.8 to 0.9 s appears 0.7 to 1.7 s later in Sift.
confirmed.fix: src/content/extract/generic.ts: when a code view's accessible textarea is not there yet, read the aria-hidden visual code lines (.react-code-lines, or an aria-hidden block with no accessible twin) as a fallback. In general, do not drop an aria-hidden block when no accessible copy of its text exists.

confirmed.verdict: Reproduced only under CPU pressure, and caused by Sift. Unthrottled at load average about 1, Sift matched the original in 5 of 5 runs (for example 3680/3680 and 3879/3879). With 2x CPU throttle (my fp2t.ts), Sift was later in 5 of 5: 6114/7447, 7360/8396, 5786/7784, 6762/7835 and 5529/7819 ms. With 4x it was later in 5 of 5, by 0.9 to 4.5 s (for example 10481/15022). A 4x poll trace shows the page's TemperatureValue visible at 13425 ms. Sift's last run before that was at 8215 ms (still 105 chars), and the next run, which added the temperature, came at 14740 ms. Cause in src/content/index.ts schedule(): once contentShown() is true, routine pacing is used. That pacing waits max(lastDur*6, backoff), or lastDur*9 when a run took over 80 ms, then requestIdleCallback with a 600 ms timeout. contentShown() also becomes true 10 s after load starts, and slow CPUs pass that while still loading. On a slow machine the page's main content shows in Sift 1 to 2 s after the original has it.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts schedule()/contentShown(): keep the loading pacing (run right after the change, not at idle) while the page is still adding large subtrees or document.readyState is not 'complete'. Do not count 'performance.now() - loadStart > 10000' as content shown while Sift still has thin content. Or cap the idle wait for big additions (many new nodes or new text) at about 200 ms.

confirmed.verdict: Confirmed. It is a high-severity regression. I ran 927358?answertab=scoredesc twice on the current build. Both runs printed [69,0,30,'https://stackoverflow.com/posts/927386/revisions']. The cards are titled 'Undo a commit & redo', 'Option 1: git reset --hard', 'How to undo a local commit' and '4 Comments'. trending gives 72/72 and modifieddesc gives 83/83. On 178325 (scoredesc) the original has 42 pre and 5 'Run code snippet'. Sift has 0 and 0, and 30 cards titled '23 Comments', '11 Comments'…, with one titled '1 Comment' that links to learn.jquery.com. On 2003505 I got 68 original pre and 7 in Sift (the claim says 1), across 34 cards. I built the committed tree (HEAD, before the round 7 fixes) into a second Chrome. It gives 69/69 on 927358 and 42/42 on 178325, so this is new. Cause: the only field in each SO answer is the share sheet's hidden, read-only input holding 'https://stackoverflow.com/a/<id>'. The old detectItems counted it as a field (withFields = 30 of 30), and that rule kept answers from becoming cards. The F738 change (copyField plus visible(f) near generic.ts line 2360) no longer counts it, so the 30 answers turn into cards. Test: I added one visible text input to each answer and switched Sift off and on. Sift went back to 69/69 pre. A control run with the same switch and no added inputs stayed at 0.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts detectItems(), add a direct guard instead of relying on the field count. Return null (walk the members) when most members hold a post body: a pre or blockquote, [itemprop=text] or .s-prose. asCard() already refuses blocks with pre or blockquote. Also narrow the F738 exemption in detectItems so only an embed code (a value starting with '<') is skipped, not a hidden share-link input.

confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, 30 items and 7 of them with a URL headline, as claimed. Item 3 is '(https://fasterthanli.me/articles/a-half-hour-to-learn-rust)' in bold, with 'A half-hour to learn Rust · 1444 points…' as a small link under it. Item 4 is '(http://blog.rust-lang.org/2015/05/15/Rust-1.0.html)' over 'Announcing Rust 1.0'. For the URL link, the line includes the title link, so a URL at least about 2.3 times as long as the title passes. Discord's 77-character URL against its 40-character title fails, and the half-hour one passes. toItem() then sorts the named links by length, so the URL wins. This is not new, but it puts the wrong headline on about 1 in 4 search results, more than polish. Medium.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts titleLink(), return false for a link whose whole text is in parentheses '(…)' or is a bare URL. That is the same 'source after a headline' rule side() already applies to the link's neighbors. Another option: in toItem(), drop such links from `named` before the longest-text sort.

confirmed.suspectedCause: The F751 change resolves the field in fieldList with liveField(a.dataset.ref). The default sync=true runs on every extraction and every refreshList, not only on the user's own keystroke. The skeptic's lead was liveField(ref, false). Even then, a swap should be adopted only when the old field was replaced in place (same form, same parent position, or the page focused the new one), never just because one same-named field is left.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced 2 of 2 times on fx/r8int-cartzero.html?v=labels. Sift's log was row1=, row1=0, row2=0, rows [] and Total $0.00. The original kept row2 ($8.00). I traced it with capture listeners on the page: focus@row2* then input@row2*=0, both synthetic, which is liveField's proxy.focus plus setValue. The labels differ in this variant, so twinOf's label match cannot fire and this is not the carry path. The pre-round-7 build (ctl on port 9477) kept row2 with no event on it, so this is a regression. confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts fieldList (~1733): look up the field with elOf, or at least liveField(ref, false). In liveField, when the old field has no form left (form === undefined), never adopt on name and type alone. Require positive evidence of an in-place swap, such as the page focusing the new field (the sift-focus path), and only proxy.focus or setValue from the user's own focus or input handlers.

confirmed.title: After an edit removes the focused field, Sift's focus repair types the same text into another field with the same label (cart quantities, number or text)
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:277-292 (twinOf falls back to any control with the same label) and src/content/index.ts:296-304 (carry writes the typed value and dispatches input)
confirmed.evidence: fx/r8int-cartzero.html has two fields labelled 'Quantity', typed text or (?v=number) number, as in most carts. Typing 0 in the first removes its row. Sift: rows [], log row1=, row1=0, row2=0, Total $0.00. The trace shows input@row2 without focus@row2, so this is the carry path, not liveField. ?v=names (different names) gives the same. The pre-round-7 build gives the same for the default, ?v=names and ?v=number variants, so this is older than round 7. The original removes only Rye loaf (rows [row2:1], $8.00). When paint() finds the focused field gone, refocus() asks twinOf(). The ref is gone, so twinOf() matches any control with the same label: the next item's Quantity. carry() then puts the old field's value there and fires input, because lastTyped > store.actAt. That sends the 0 to the page.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r8int/cartzero.ts sift '?v=number' prints rows []. Add 'orig' as the first argument for the original, which prints rows [row2:1].
confirmed.suspectedCause: carry() is meant for the same field after a re-render. It should only write when the twin stands for the same page element (same data-ref, or one adopted under the rules for a replaced field). A label-only twin may take focus but must never take the typed text.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on ?v=names, ?v=number and the default variant: rows [] and row2=0 each time. In ?v=names and ?v=number the trace shows input@row2*=0 with no focus@row2, and the names differ, so liveField cannot match. At t+100 ms Sift had r5=0 focused. At t+400 ms Sift's r7 (the other 'Quantity') was focused with value 0, and the page's row2 had received it. That is refocusNow, then twinOf's label fallback, then carry() writing spot.value and dispatching input. The ctl build gave the same result for names, number and default, so this is older than round 7. The original removes only Rye loaf (rows [row2:1], $8.00) in all variants.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts carry() (~296): write the value and dispatch input only when twin.dataset.ref === spot.ref (or the ref was legitimately adopted). A label-only twin from twinOf may take focus and the caret, never the typed text.

confirmed.suspectedCause: The 'still in it' test should also accept focus inside the field's own suggestion sheet: compare the original shadow.activeElement (before the suggestAnchor() swap) against '.sheet.suggest', not `a`.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced 3 of 3 times on users.rust-lang.org/latest. After Search, typing 'lifetime' and Enter, Sift shows 6 results under the field. ArrowDown focuses 'Lifetime issue - expected lifetime…'. After a page mutation (3 divs appended), one routine run fires (runs 20 to 21). Sift's sheet is then gone and focus is back in the input. The page's own .search-menu results are still visible with 6 links, so Sift differs from the original. With no mutation, the list and focus stayed for 9 s. The code agrees: in fieldList, `a` is swapped for suggestAnchor() when focus is in the sheet, so `a === shadow.activeElement` is false in the post-action branch and it returns undefined. confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts fieldList (~1729-1743): keep the original shadow.activeElement and treat focus inside '.sheet.suggest' as being at the field. Use `(a === shadow.activeElement || shadow.activeElement?.closest('.sheet.suggest'))` in the panel condition instead of `a === shadow.activeElement`.
